obligation: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act privacy and safeguards
basis: The bank is a financial institution holding nonpublic personal information of about 16,000 deposit customers. Section 501(b) is implemented for national banks through the OCC's Interagency Guidelines (N52-R02)

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards (OCC)
citation: 12 CFR Part 30, Appendix B, with Supplement A
basis: Section I.A applies the Guidelines to customer information maintained by or on behalf of national banks; the bank holds an OCC national bank charter. No size exemption; the program must be appropriate to size and complexity (II.A)

obligation: Interagency Guidelines (Federal Reserve version) for the holding company
basis: The holding company has no operations or customer information of its own, so its duty is met through the bank's program

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule (bank)
basis: Applies to all national banks (53.1(c)): 36-hour notice to the OCC after a notification incident is determined; bank service providers must notify the bank (53.4)

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification (holding company)
basis: Cris Santos Company is a U.S. bank holding company; the same 36-hour duty applies if a notification incident affects it

obligation: FDIC computer-security incident notification
basis: The bank's primary federal regulator is the OCC, so Part 53 applies instead

obligation: Suspicious activity reports
basis: National banks must file SARs; the bank has a BSA/AML Officer, a SAR log and BSA procedures

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule (GLBA)
basis: The rule covers financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction; the bank is supervised by the OCC

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation
basis: Not New York-chartered or licensed

obligation: SEC Regulation S-P (2024 amendments)
basis: No SEC-registered broker-dealer, investment company or investment adviser in the group

obligation: SEC Regulation S-ID (Identity Theft Red Flags)
basis: No SEC-registered broker-dealer, investment company or investment adviser in the group

obligation: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668
citation: NAIC Model #668, as adopted by states
basis: No insurance agency or insurance license in the group

obligation: SEC public-company cybersecurity disclosure
basis: Neither the bank nor the holding company has securities registered with the SEC

obligation: NCUA security program and cyber incident notification
basis: The bank is a national bank, not a federally insured credit union

obligation: OCC heightened standards for large banks
basis: Applies at average total consolidated assets of $50 billion or more; the bank has $510 million in total assets

obligation: Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B (discrimination; adverse action notices)
basis: The bank extends business and consumer credit and gives adverse action notices, including for applications scored by the AI credit model

obligation: CFPB small business lending data collection
basis: About 350 small business applications a year, far fewer than the covered-transaction threshold that defines a covered financial institution

obligation: Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E
basis: Consumer wires sent through Fedwire are excluded from the definition of electronic fund transfer; consumer ACH and online bill payments are covered and sit outside the SSP's security scope

obligation: Florida UCC Article 4A (funds transfers; security procedures)
basis: Florida law governs the bank's funds transfer agreements with customers, which set the agreed security procedure

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification)
basis: The bank holds personal information of Florida residents

obligation: PCI DSS through the card processor agreement
basis: Debit cards are issued and processed by the card processor; card data stays in the processor's services and the ATMs

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
basis: Final rule not published; tracked for planning

obligation: Bank holding company and change of control approvals
basis: The holding company acquisition received Federal Reserve approval; a later acquirer of control gives the Federal Reserve 60 days' notice

obligation: State AI laws (for example Colorado SB26-189)
basis: The bank lends only to Florida businesses
